לא נמצאה אפליקציה רשמית של החברה להגנת ה: No official app by SPNI/the Israel Trails Committee for the Israel National Trail was found (as of November 2026). No apps named 'Shvilist', 'Israel Trail Guide by Jacob Saar' or 'INT by Eli' were found. No dedicated app for trail angels or water caching was found.
התמונה בשוק (נובמבר 2026): יש בדיוק אפלי: The market picture (November 2026): there is exactly one dedicated Israel National Trail app – 'Israel National Trail' by Lior Boyango – free, offline, with sections, water, campsites and self-managed trail angels, and a high rating (4.5–4.7). It is a good field companion but has almost no planning layer: no daily itinerary, no water/heat/daylight calculations, no journal, no export. Against it stand general map apps: Israel Hiking Map/Mapeak (the best map in Israel, open source, route planning and recording, but offline costs ILS 99.90 per year and zero trail logistics), and Amud Anan (a huge community POI database but a 3.1 rating, crashes, abandoned iOS, paid maps). The global apps (Wikiloc, AllTrails, Komoot, HiiKER, FarOut) cover the trail partially or as user routes, lock offline/alerts/live sharing behind subscriptions of ILS 80–300 per year, and have no Hebrew, angels, caches or official overnight campsites – although FarOut offers an excellent model of dated comments on every water point, AllTrails/Off-Road offer live location sharing, and HiiKER a division into stages with amenities. SPNI has not released an official app; the official information (52 maps, angel list, route changes) is scattered across PDFs and web pages. The recurring complaints everywhere: paid offline, battery drain, outdated angel phone numbers, water info going stale, no planner, no watch support, and apps that depend on a single developer. The big gap: no tool connects planning (daily, water, caches, angels, Shabbat, daylight, heat/floods) with field guidance and logging – and that is exactly what our PWA is already starting to do.

נחשים ועקרבים: לבחור משטח לינה חשוף ונקי: Snakes and scorpions: choose a bare, clean sleeping spot, shake out shoes/sleeping bag in the morning, don't put your hands into crevices, use a headlamp at night, closed shoes. Bites are rare and death is very rare – in case of a bite: rest, call 101/MDA and INPA *3639.

Do not sleep in a closed firing zone; the Israel Trail itself is coordinated, but detours from it may enter a closed zone.

חניוני לילה ללא תשלום של רט\"ג (מעל 100: Free INPA overnight campsites (over 100 nationwide, many along the Israel Trail): no advance coordination and no fee; amplification/music prohibited; do not arrive after dark (harms wildlife); large groups – a portable toilet stall per ~40 people; pack out all trash.
חופים: לינה מוסדרת בחופי קמפינג (בכנרת –: Beaches: regulated camping at camping beaches (on the Kinneret – Kinneret Cities Association beaches, paid; on the Mediterranean – a few declared overnight campsites, and the state is expanding 'regulated camping' along the coast). There is no uniform law – the rules depend on the local authority/INPA; beach campfires only where permitted.
שמורות טבע וגנים לאומיים: לינה מותרת אך: Nature reserves and national parks: sleeping is allowed only at declared overnight campsites (paid or free). Do not sleep, pitch a tent or walk at night outside the campsites. In the Negev most of the trail passes through reserves – so in practice, lodging in the south is only at the overnight campsites marked on maps and signage.
שטח פתוח שאינו שמורה/גן לאומי/יער מוכרז: Open land that is not a reserve/national park/declared forest (e.g. the coastal plain and parts of the north): no blanket prohibition, but do not sleep on private/agricultural land without permission, not in firing zones, and not near water sources (leave the springs to wildlife at night – INPA places campsites ~800 m from springs).
חיות בר: צבועים, זאבים ותנים אינם תוקפים: Wildlife: hyenas, wolves and jackals do not attack humans (apart from rare rabies cases; per INPA, no attack by a striped hyena in the wild has ever been documented in Israel), but they are drawn to food – store food sealed and not in the tent/near your head; a wolf was documented tearing a sleeping bag while searching for food. Do not feed animals.

מים: לא לשתות ממעיינות/גבים ללא טיהור; ע: Water: do not drink from springs/rock pools without treatment; INPA water tankers at the southern campsites (Yehoram, Shehoret, Raham-Etek, Be'er Milhan, Nahal Tzihor, Nahal Barak, Nekarot West, Nahal Gevanim, Hod Akev, Mitzpe Makhtesh – autumn 2025) are for drinking only, not for washing; the authority recommends 4–6 litres per person per day (6–7 in summer/the south).
מלאכי שביל: חינם/תרומה 20–80 ₪; חניוני ל: Trail angels: free/donation 20–80 ILS; free overnight campsites; paid INPA campsites 47–76 ILS; Kinneret camping ~50 ILS; shared Bedouin tent 50–150 ILS; hostel dorm 80–180 ILS; IYHA hostel ~180–270 ILS per person in a double (360–535 ILS per couple); field school 237–274 ILS per person incl. breakfast; zimmer 350–900 ILS per couple.
הדלקת אש בשמורות ובגנים לאומיים מותרת אך: Lighting fires in reserves and national parks is allowed only at overnight campsites and in designated spots; gathering/burning local vegetation (even a dry branch) is prohibited – bring wood/gas in advance. At free campsites cooking on a gas stove is allowed. On heat-wave days and under fire-service orders – total fire ban even at approved spots; check INPA updates.
